title: GPU page-pool churn causing OOM cascades and KV cache integrity drift — patch, rollout, and customer remediation
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments reported sudden GPU OOM cascades over the last 36 hours accompanied by KV cache entries becoming stale or failing to reconcile. Initial triage showed frequent small allocations and frees inside the GPU page-pool leading to fragmentation and an unexpected allocator path that marked KV handles as 'in-flight' but then leaked their backing pages. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, the short-term mitigation applied to live fleets, the runtime patch (PR linked), rollback/rollforward strategy, customer communications, and next steps for long-term resilience.

Root cause (high level): The page-pool reclaim path would sometimes race with the KV cache snapshot reconciler when workloads exhibited high session churn and large prefix cache growth. The race could leave a KV index pointing at a page index that had been returned to the free list but not yet zeroed; under heavy allocation pressure this caused reuse of the same physical page while KV metadata still referenced the previous contents resulting in corruption and then a chain of allocator errors that triggered OOM evacuations on the GPU.

Impact: High — 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated experienced service degradation with tail latency spikes and a sustained elevated error rate for 5–40 minutes before mitigation. Hosted customers saw a small % of requests return corrupted generations (detected and rolled back by service-side checks). Private deployments reported intermittent GPU memory exhaustion with degraded throughput.

Mitigation applied (short-term hotfix): Deployed immediate policy-change to reduce aggressive page reuse and enabled conservative backpressure on new KV snapshots. This reduced OOM frequency by >90% for affected customers while we validated the runtime fix. See mitigation rollout notes in timeline and PR history.

Patch summary: The runtime patch (PR #11842) introduces an atomic epoch counter for page allocations and a delayed zeroing guarantee for pages reclaimed from the page-pool before they can be referenced by KV index snapshots. It also hardens the KV snapshot reconciler to treat 'recently freed' pages as transient and forces a lightweight copy-on-write if a race is detected. Memory overhead is slightly increased if the copy-on-write path is exercised.

Testing and verification: Patch validated with unit tests simulating high session churn, stress harness reproducing previous failure trace, and a canary fleet run on Dedicated with synthetic workloads matching customer token distribution. Canary passed for 72 hours with no OOMs and no KV inconsistencies. Load test artifacts and memory heatmaps attached.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge PR after two engineer approvals and signoff from SRE. 2) Gradual rollout to Hosted low-traffic region (10% traffic) for 12h. 3) Expand to Dedicated canary nodes for affected customers with opt-in. 4) Full rollout across Dedicated/Hosted after 72h of clean metrics. Private deployments: provide patch bundle and step-by-step upgrade playbook; coordinate with onsite engineers for rolling restart windows.

Customer communications: Drafted customer notes and incident summary for affected customers; offered scheduled maintenance windows for Dedicated and Private customers; provided investigative logs and diagnostic dumps. Engineering lead will join the next support sync for high-touch customers.

Postmortem action items (short list): - Add stronger invariants and sanitizers in the allocator for debug builds. - Add extended KV snapshot reconciliation metrics and alarms. - Explore compacting page allocator to reduce fragmentation under churn. - Prioritize an RFC for safer copy-on-write semantics in the KV cache.

Links and artifacts: see links field for PR, canary dashboards, and incident report references.
